types.description: Abstract base validator — the shared root subtype concrete validators specialize. Carries the @min/@max bounds attrs but enforces no rule of its own.

children.name: min
children.description: Minimum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

children.name: max
children.description: Maximum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

types.description: Fails when the value is null/empty (NOT NULL). Equivalent to @required on the owning field.
types.whenToUse: A field must be present (NOT NULL). Declare it instead of hand-writing a null/empty check.

types.description: Bounds string length / collection size via @min/@max.
types.whenToUse: Bound a string's length or a collection's size. Use @min/@max instead of hand-written guards.

children.name: min
children.description: Minimum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

children.name: max
children.description: Maximum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

types.description: Requires the value match a regular expression (@pattern).
types.whenToUse: A string must match a pattern (email, slug, code). Set @pattern instead of hand-writing the regex test.

children.name: min
children.description: Minimum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

children.name: max
children.description: Maximum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

children.name: pattern
children.description: Regular expression the value must match.

types.description: Bounds a numeric value's magnitude via @min/@max.
types.whenToUse: Bound a number's magnitude. Use @min/@max instead of hand-written range checks.

children.name: min
children.description: Minimum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

children.name: max
children.description: Maximum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

types.description: Bounds the element count of an array-valued field via @min/@max.
types.whenToUse: Bound the element count of an array field. Use @min/@max instead of a hand-written length check.

children.name: min
children.description: Minimum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

children.name: max
children.description: Maximum allowed value (length, numeric value, or array element count depending on the validator subtype).

types.description: Cross-field ordering: requires two sibling fields of the owning entity stand in a relational order (@left @op @right), e.g. current_hp <= max_hp or expires_at > created_at. Entity-scoped; references fields by name. Backends derive the rule (CHECK constraint, cross-field assertion) — no raw expression is stored.
types.whenToUse: Two sibling fields must stand in an order (start <= end, currentHp <= maxHp). Declare it instead of hand-writing the cross-field assertion.
types.rules: @left and @right must name fields of the owning entity. @op is one of gt/gte/lt/lte/ne/eq. The comparison is null-tolerant where the backend's relational operator is (SQL: a NULL operand yields no violation).

children.name: left
children.description: Name of the left-hand field of the owning entity.

children.name: op
children.description: Relational operator: gt (>), gte (>=), lt (<), lte (<=), ne (<>), eq (=).

children.name: right
children.description: Name of the right-hand field of the owning entity.

types.description: One-directional conditional presence: when the gating field (@when) equals @equals, the target field (@field) must be present (NOT NULL); otherwise @field is unconstrained. Mirrors JSON Schema dependentRequired / Rails validates_presence_of :x, if:. Entity-scoped; references fields by name.
types.whenToUse: A field becomes required only when another field has a given value. Declare it instead of conditional validation code.
types.rules: @field and @when must name fields of the owning entity. @equals is the gating value, compared against @when's value (rendered per @when's field subtype — boolean true/false, enum/string literal, numeric literal).

children.name: field
children.description: Name of the field that becomes required when the condition holds.

children.name: when
children.description: Name of the gating field whose value triggers the requirement.

children.name: equals
children.description: The gating value; when @when equals this, @field must be present.

types.description: Biconditional presence: the target field (@field) is present (NOT NULL) if and only if the gating field (@when) equals @equals. Models paired flag/companion-column invariants, e.g. used_at present iff is_used=true. Entity-scoped; references fields by name.
types.whenToUse: A field must be present exactly when a condition holds, absent otherwise (biconditional). Declare it instead of hand-written presence logic.
types.rules: @field and @when must name fields of the owning entity. @equals is rendered per @when's field subtype. Stricter than requiredWhen — also forbids @field when the condition is false.

children.name: field
children.description: Name of the field whose presence is governed by the condition.

children.name: when
children.description: Name of the gating field.

children.name: equals
children.description: The gating value; @field is present exactly when @when equals this.

types.description: Cardinality of presence: at least one of the named fields (@fields) must be present (NOT NULL). Entity-scoped; references fields by name (same @fields-by-name pattern as identity.*).
types.whenToUse: At least one of several fields must be present (email or phone). Declare it instead of hand-written OR-presence checks.
types.rules: @fields names two or more fields of the owning entity. Satisfied when any one of them is non-null.

children.name: fields
children.description: Names of the candidate fields; at least one must be present.
